The doormat pattern (seen on Tuesday and Wednesday, not on Friday–Sunday) strongly suggests weekday daycare drop-off/pickup. Today (Tuesday) the doormat moved to entry hook at 19:17, consistent with afternoon pickup. The board book at playmat at 08:40 suggests morning play before daycare. The sippy cup at sink at 12:21 is a generic lunchtime item. The fork at table at 11:36 and waste bin at counter at 11:46 are mundane. The wall clock at counter at 16:14 is generic. The evidence strongly supports a full-time child with weekday daycare.

hypotheses.persona: Single adult with a child visiting part-time (e.g., every other weekend or weekdays).
hypotheses.rationale: Child items appear on all eight days, which is less typical for part-time care unless the adult works from home or the child is in daycare on weekdays. The doormat pattern (not seen on Friday–Sunday) could still fit a part-time schedule, but the consistent presence of child items every day makes this less likely than full-time care. The new evidence (board book at playmat on Tuesday morning) does not contradict this hypothesis but does not strengthen it either.
